items: **Both were at ASHG 2026 in Montréal:** Eric exhibited at booth **1723**; Meteor posted "what happens after the image?… we are in Montréal this week". They did not meet.
**Single-cell scale:** Eric was head architect of NVIDIA BioNeMo's single-cell data loader (**SCDL**, built for billions of cells) — Amos's spatial/single-cell data is exactly that kind of load.
**Both are genomics-method scientists with Nature Biotechnology papers:** Eric co-authored the 2018 *vg* toolkit paper; Amos has published CosmoSort (SLACS) work in Nature Biotech.
**Cancer genomics:** Eric's PhD (Cambridge + NIH/NCI) was the largest genomic study of the Chernobyl Tissue Bank (400+ whole genomes); Meteor works on the tumor microenvironment.
No shared school or employer: Eric studied at **UT Austin** and **Cambridge**; Amos at **UC Berkeley** and **SNU**. No co-authorship found.

lead_with.title: Partnership, not a sale
lead_with.text: Eric was clear: no wet lab, so not a customer. Lead with a **compute partnership** — SLACS isolates the cells, EarthFrame accelerates the downstream sequencing and analysis.

lead_with.title: His NVIDIA single-cell and genomics depth
lead_with.text: 5.5 years at NVIDIA (to Oct 2025): Parabricks contributor, led BioNeMo protein-structure NIMs (AlphaFold2, Boltz-2, MMseqs2), architect of the **SCDL single-cell loader**. EarthFrame boxes run Parabricks on RTX Pro GPUs — **WGS alignment + calling in under 20 minutes**.

lead_with.title: Data stays on site
lead_with.text: EarthFrame sells **sovereign, on-prem** compute. Hospitals and pharma sending clinical tissue to Meteor care about where data lives — a joint "sample to result, data never leaves" story.

person.name: Eric T. Dawson
person.text: President & Co-Founder of **EarthFrame** (Nov 2025–, Austin TX) and Founder of **Phileal, LLC** (Oct 2025–; bioinformatics and genomics infrastructure, accelerated workflows, custom software and consulting). Before that **5.5 years at NVIDIA**: Bioinformatics Scientist (2020–23), then Senior Scientist (2023–Oct 2025) — Parabricks contributor, led BioNeMo protein-structure NIMs (AlphaFold2, Boltz-2, MMseqs2), head architect of the BioNeMo single-cell data loader (SCDL) for billions of cells. PhD at the **University of Cambridge** and **NIH/NCI** (2015–2020) in Richard Durbin's group at Sanger with Stephen Chanock: the largest genomic study of the Chernobyl Tissue Bank (400+ WGS), vg-based SV calling, HPV coinfection detection. Undergrad at UT Austin, worked at TACC and won the Student Cluster Competition. Teaches Wellcome courses. 1,672 LinkedIn followers; X @erictdawson; GitHub edawson.

company.text: EarthFrame Corporation is a Public Benefit Corporation (Austin, TX; founded Nov 2025) building **sovereign, sustainable AI**: local GPU compute and storage that cut AI's energy footprint and keep sensitive data on site, with a genomics focus (Sovereign Biobank Reference Design; NVIDIA Parabricks, Nextflow). Systems: Ember, EarthFrame 1, Mesa. Cofounders: **Eric T. Dawson** (President), **Prof. Keolu Fox** (UC San Diego; Indigenous Data Sovereignty) and **Yousuf W. Rajput**; Head of Product **Juvenson Edouard**. Eric's separate **Phileal, LLC** offers bioinformatics infrastructure, accelerated workflows and custom software/consulting — the vehicle for one-off analysis projects.

history.text: LinkedIn, around Oct 16, 2026 (as Amos). Eric: “Would be happy to talk about collaboration opportunities (we could probably accelerate that work with our hardware / software). We don't do any wet lab though so wouldn't be customers. Come by booth 1723 and chat” — at **ASHG 2026**, Montréal. He gave **eric@earthframe.com**. Jenny Park emailed him on Oct 21 (cc Amos); opened once, no reply.

industry.title: GPU acceleration reaches single-cell data
industry.text: NVIDIA's single-cell AI Blueprint (rapids-singlecell) claims 676x faster UMAP and 70x faster PCA on a 1M-cell dataset. Spatial multi-omics is next in line — data volumes keep growing.

industry.title: Sovereign data in genomics
industry.text: Data-sovereignty and on-prem genomics are a rising theme (biobanks, Indigenous data, national programs). Keolu Fox, EarthFrame's cofounder, is a leading voice on Indigenous genomic data sovereignty.

talking_points: You said EarthFrame could accelerate our work — which step would you attack first: sequencing analysis after SLACS, image processing, or the integration of both?
What does a SLACS spatial multi-omics dataset look like on an Ember or Mesa box — hours instead of days?
Your new **Phindex** annotates germline/somatic VCFs in under 10 seconds — could it slot into the analysis of SLACS-isolated tumor regions?
Your Sovereign Biobank design runs Parabricks and Nextflow on site — could it be a reference setup we recommend to US hospital and pharma partners who can't send data to the cloud?
Would a joint application note or webinar (SLACS sample prep + EarthFrame compute) be useful for both of us before AGBT or AACR?
Who in your network — ex-NVIDIA BioNeMo/Parabricks, Sanger, NCI — works on spatial or tumor-microenvironment data and should know about SLACS?
What would a small first project look like this quarter — one public dataset, benchmarked end to end?
Should a first project run through **Phileal** (consulting) or **EarthFrame** (hardware) — which do you want in front?
